tagline: Two plantation histories off a two-mile road.
intro: From Whipple Road, Long Point Road runs toward US 17 through Mount Pleasant. At Snee Farm, the Charles Pinckney National Historic Site preserves part of a working plantation once used as Pinckney’s country retreat. Its present house belongs to a later owner.

A separate visit to Boone Hall follows another plantation history. There, surviving brick cabins housed enslaved workers and then sharecroppers into the 1940s, while the main house dates from the twentieth century. The small buildings carry the longer record.

moments.title: Charles Pinckney National Historic Site
moments.text: At Snee Farm, a coastal cottage with a full-width porch stands where later owners replaced the Pinckney-era buildings.

moments.title: Boone Hall
moments.text: Brick cabins preserve the homes of enslaved workers and later sharecroppers, beside an estate whose main house was built much later.
